ns2:section.sectionText: The course begins with a close look a t decolonization, the process through which European colonies in Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean emerged as independent nation states. We will examine the transition from a world dominated by European imperial powers, particularly Britain, to the Cold War world dominated by two superpowers with competing ideologies and nuclear weaponry-- the United States and the Soviet Union. We will examine the rise and fall of great superpowers not from the imperial capitals of London, Paris, Washington D.C., or Moscow, but from the edges of empire--from places like Vietnam, Iran, Algeria, South Africa, and Jamaica.
